Commentary.Commentary: 220 to win. 20 overs is the time allotted. Whose side are you on? I suggest do not be on any. Take a break and come back with some coffee. You may not get time to take another break when the run fest resumes. Stay tuned...

Should we talk about the bowlers? Poor guys, we should. It is a day when 4-0-37-1 are considered to be decent. Everyone went for plenty and to be honest, India might think that the Kiwis are 20 runs short because of the run rate slowing down with the wickets in the middle. The fielding was a let down, so that is a cause of concern.

India did threaten to come back though. They managed to slow down proceedings with the wickets of Williamson and Daryl Mitchell but then the unbeaten 24-run stand in just 11 balls for the 7th wicket has given the Kiwis some edge. Probably.

Crash, bang, pummel, slap, pound, clobber, clunk. That is what we got to see for a major portion of the innings. The move to select Tim Seifert worked for the Kiwis and he responded brilliantly, putting the Indians to the sword. He single-handedly took charge of the situation, smashing 84 from just 43 balls, with 7 fours and 6 sixes. The rest just about managed to touch 15 boundaries, that too, due to the explosion at the end.
Highest score for New Zealand against India in T20Is. Highest for the Kiwis at this ground as well. Boy, we have seen a run fest. And I daresay, it has just started.

FOUR! Not sure if that was in the gap or due to Dhawan slipping, it went to the boundary. A full toss and on off, Santner goes down on one knee and slogs it. It is hit well and it seems in the gap. However, Dhawan out there slips leaving him no chance to stop the ball. Perfect end to the innings. 9 from the last three balls and 12 from the over. NEW ZEALAND END WITH 219!
Another slower ball and it is shorter in length, Scott pulls it all along the ground but to the man at deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! New Zealand though have started the second half well. All power this. Kuggeleijn sits back and waits for the slower ball to arrive. He smashes it through extra cover and into the fence.
Good change in length and in pace. Short and outside off, it is slapped down to long off for a run. India have won the first part of the final over.
Slower ball outside off, SK is a touch early into the shot, it goes off the inner half through square leg for a single.
A full toss on off, Santner swings his bat across the line sends it to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Khaleel Ahmed to bowl the last over. False start first up, stops before the crease as he looks at his field...

SIX! All the way! 17 runs from the penultimate over! Kuggeleijn is playing an excellent cameo here. This is a top shot! It is full and wide once again outside off. SK lofts it over covers, the timing is such that it has carried all the way. 220 is now possible. One over to go, 13 needed.
Once again the batter shuffles right across and Kumar falls into the trap. He tries to hit the stumps but bowls it down leg. Wide signaled.

FOUR! Clever, very clever! Kuggeleijn moves right across and Bhuvi bowls it wide outside off, very wide I should write. But SK smartly opens the face of the bat and then guides it past the short third man fielder who puts in a dive and into the fence. Second in the over, so despite the wicket, runs are flowing.
The slower one, it is quite slow and outside off. SK throws his bat at it but misses.

EDGY FOUR! New Zealand won't mind how they come as long as they come. This is frustrating though for India. Short and outside off, Kuggeleijn slashes at it, it goes off the outside edge and through the vacant slip region to the third man boundary.
Slower one, on a length and angling away from the batsman, Santner pushes it gently towards point for a run.
Scott Kuggeleijn is in next.

OUT! Another one straight up in the air and Khaleel just about takes it. Taylor departs so the drop does not cost India a lot. It is outside off and on a length. Taylor looks to drag his shot on the leg side. Only manages a top edge. Another skier for an Indian fielder. Khaleel at short fine leg settles under it and just about holds onto the catch. It was actually a good call. Three fielders were circling under it - Khaleel, Dhoni and Rishabh Pant at square leg. But Khaleel calls for it, stands still and takes it. Oops... almost drops it as the ball pops out but it sticks in his hand. Can India now keep the Kiwis under 210?
Wide! It's too wide outside off, left alone.
A gentle length delivery wide outside off, Taylor cuts it through point and takes a run. 10 runs and a wicket from Hardik's last over, was expensive today. Conceded 51.
Mitchell Santner is the new batsman with 13 balls left.

OUT! Colin departs off a full toss. But a lot of credit has to be given to the catch there, especially on a day where India have been lackluster in the field. Another high full toss to Colin de Grandhomme. He pulls it hard but gets it very high in the air. For a second it seems like the ball has cleared the ropes but then with the parabolic trajectory ending, a fielder comes in sight. It is the substitute Mohammed Siraj who does really well to settle under it. He also has to keep a track of where the ropes are. Judges it really well and takes a tumbling catch to his left.
A low full toss, it is flicked through square leg for a run.

In the air... dropped! Karthik has put down another sitter. This was really easy. Firstly it was a full toss on middle, Taylor fails to time it well. He has more height on this than distance. It goes straight towards deep mid-wicket. Karthik there tries to take it but drops. Hard to say how? The ball went straight in and then straight out. Hit his hands, went right through, into the bread basket and down. Two taken by the batsmen. India have been really poor in the field today. Will Taylor make them pay now? He can be dangerous.
Top response! A yorker outside off, all Taylor can do is jam it out towards the bowler.

SIX! That just crosses the ropes! Right in the zone for Taylor. Full and on middle, he hits it high up in the air towards mid-wicket. It is in the gap though and it is hit well enough to clear the ropes. Ideal start to the over, pressure on the bowler.
Hardik Pandya to bowl the 18th.
Turns it off his pads through mid-wicket for a single. A good comeback in the last three balls by Kumar. 11 in total from the over.
Very full and outside off, it's forced from the crease to extra cover and it's fielded inside the ring. The single is not prevented.
Length again, once again Taylor takes it from outside off and drills it down to long on for one. 9 runs so far.
SIX! Wow, that's flat and all the way! Kumar serves it on a length and way wide outside off. Ross reaches out for it and rifles it all the way over extra cover.

High in the air... SAFE! Taylor fetches a length ball from outside off and swings his bat across the line. It flies off the top edge and falls in no man's land at cow corner. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs.

Keeps it fuller and wider outside off, Taylor walks across, flashes his bat at it but misses. Not given a wide and Rosco ain't too pleased. Not a bad call there by the umpire as Taylor was shuffling across too much.
Bhuvneshwar Kumar is back on to bowl at the death.

A flatter and shorter one to end! Taylor rocks back and looks to pull. It goes off the lower portion of the bat as it did not bounce as anticipated. It goes towards mid-wicket for another run. Finishes his spell with a brilliant over. 5 runs and the big wicket of Williamson. His figures too are good in the context of the game. It reads 4-0-35-1.
Another googly and once again Colin does not pick it. He looks to go hard again but once again it is off the inner half through mid-wicket for another single.
Nicely bowled! The length is perfect and it is on off, a little turn. Taylor pushes it towards covers for a run.
Colin is going after it straightaway! It is the googly, he does not pick it. Looks to go hard through the off side but it goes off the inner half towards long on for a run.
Tosses it up on off, Taylor strokes it down to long off and gets to the other end.
Colin de Grandhomme is the new man in.

OUT! Well, Rosco has arrived but Williamson departs! India are making a good comeback here. Chahal drops it short and on middle, Williamson moves back to pull it over mid-wicket but it seems the ball arrives a bit late off the surface which results in him mistiming the shot. As a result, Kane doesn't get enough meat behind it and Hardik in the deep takes the catch easily. Both the set batsmen gone, two new batters in the middle, can the Black Caps still finish on a high?
Ross Taylor arrives.

OUT! Yes, it is clean as a whistle! The dangerous Mitchell has been given his marching orders. Pandya finishes a very expensive over well. He bowls the full one and it might be the slower one. DM looks to clear the long on fence but it is not off the middle. Still for a second it did seem like it would clear the ropes. Dinesh Karthik though who dropped one earlier, takes it but then realizes he is losing his balance. Throws it up, crosses the ropes, comes back in and then takes it with a dive. He though is not sure and Mitchell continues completing his run. The umpires now take it upstairs. Replays show the confusion in Karthik's mind. While coming in to take that catch, his left leg touches the ropes. However, it is off when he dives. So it is pretty safe. Then they check for the no ball, that too is fine. This is what India have to do if they are to stem the run flow. PICK WICKETS!
Has that been taken? Karthik is not sure though, the umpires have taken it upstairs.
Mitchell shuffles right across. Pandya looks to bowl it on the stumps but sprays it down the leg side. Wide signaled.
Another couple! Mitchell strokes it wide of the long off. They run the first one hard and then go for a second. The fielder misfields and makes the second easy for the batsmen.

Changes his length and goes very full on off, Williamson strokes it towards mid off and goes for a run. The fielder misses his shy at the non-striker's end. Mitchell is ready for for the second but Williamson is not. They settle for a single.
SIX! 230 is possible if he keeps hitting like this! Another short one and Williamson picks the length early. He once again pulls it right off the meat and into the square leg stand.

SIX! Dispatched! Williamson surely expected a short and he got one there. He was in position quickly, hits it right off the middle and over the square leg fence. 150 up and more than 5 overs to go. 220?
Wide outside off again, this time though it is inside the wide line. Mitchell does get bat to it and hits it through cover for a run.
WIDE! False start for him. He tries a slower one but it is way wide outside off. It has been wided. DM did shuffle across and looked to cut but it was very wide.
Hardik Pandya is back.
Sits down on one knee and and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket. Krunal does well in the deep and saves two for his team.
Tossed up ball on middle, Williamson turns it through mid-wicket and immediately calls for two. Completes it with ease.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
A googly around off, turning back in, Williamson moves back to keep it out at the last moment. The ball rolls in the gap towards short third man and they take a run.
Short and outside off, cut straight to cover-point.
Flatter and shorter on middle, punched wide of mid on for a couple of runs.

FOUR! Aerially past the bowler for a boundary. A length ball angling back into the batsman, Mitchell brings down a straight bat and slaps it past the bowler. Khaleel ducks there to avoid any harm to himself. 11 from the over along with a wicket.
Excellent delivery. Khaleel bends his back and digs in a short ball on off, Mitchell goes on his toes and defends it down safely.
Debutant Daryl Mitchell is in.

OUT! Timberrrr... No century for Tim Seifert. It's an excellent delivery. Khaleel spears in a fuller length ball on off, Tim remains back to heave it over the leg side but gets an inside edge onto the stumps. India will be relieved to see his back. He was going bonkers in his knock of 84 from 43 balls.

Well bowled this time. Drops it short but takes the pace off it. Williamson skips down the track but is deceived in pace. Somehow manages to get it away off the bottom half towards mid on and takes a run.
SIX! Khaleel runs in from 'round the wicket and angles in a short ball around off, Williamson uses the angle to his advantage. Rocks back and rockets his pull over mid-wicket.
Slower delivery, short and outside off, Williamson pushes it from the crease but finds the cover fielder.
Khaleel Ahmed is back on. 0/25 from 2 overs so far.

SIX! That has gone deep into the crowd. Great finish to the over by Seifert. Full floated on middle, Tim gets the opportunity to sit down and hoick it over mid-wicket. 13 from the over, New Zealand are cruising.
FOUR! Extra flight on this occasion, it lands full and wide outside off, Seifert reaches out for it and crunches his drive through covers for a boundary.
Shortish and pulled to deep mid-wicket for another single in this over.
Bowls it with a quick-arm action, it's short and on leg,  Seifert gets back and forces it down to long on for a run.
Very full, around off, Williamson initially looks to sweep but then adjusts on seeing the length. Pushes the ball to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.

DROPPED BY DK! Oh dear, what have you done? A full flighted ball on middle, Seifert kneels for another big shot but this time he has skied it up towards long on. Karthik runs forward but drops a dolly. Two taken. Krunal has bowled out, 4-0-37-1, a decent spell given the hammering other bowlers have received so far.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single.
Goes on the back foot and punches it through covers for one.
SIX! Just over the fielder! Seifert is putting on a show here. Full and floated on off, Tim plays an inside-out shot and it goes flying over wide long off for back-to-back maximums.
SIX! High and handsome! Krunal drops it short around off, Seifert wears his skates to run down the track and dismisses it over mid-wicket for a maximum.
Flatter and shorter on off, Williamson moves back and eases it through covers for a run.

Loopy and full on off, Williamson pushes at it and gets an inside edge past the stumps to short fine leg. They steal a run as Bhuvneshwar scores a direct hit at the striker's end. Nothing doing. 9 from Chahal's first over.
Full and on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.
Quicker and fuller on middle, Tim gets across the stumps and slogs it over backward square leg. Two taken.

FOUR! Finds the gap with perfection! A shortish ball on middle and off, Seifert jumps inside the crease to play the reverse-batted shot and does so aerially through the gap between point and short third man.
Another short ball around off, Williamson goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket. A single has been taken. The replays show that it reached the batsman late and Kane nearly lost his balance.
Drops it short and quick on off, Williamson taps it down to short third man.
Yuzvendra Chahal is introduced into the attack.
Shortish and outside off, cut through cover-point for one. First decent over for India today, 3 runs and a wicket from it!

Krunal is not happy! He's complaining to the umpire. A mistimed shot by Williamson and the ball lobs back in the direction of the bowler. Krunal attempts for the catch with a dive but collides with Seifert. The bowler gets up angry and appeals while seeing the umpire. Obstructing the field? Don't think so. Tim has every right to hold his ground.
The batsman plays a sweep shot. They pick up a single.
Arm ball on middle, skidding into the batsman from a shorter side, Seifert moves back and hits it on the off side. Not in the gap.
Kane Williamson is the new batsman.

OUT! Munro holes out. Krunal shows the courage to flight it up and lands it on the fuller side on middle. Colin tries to clear long on but gets more height than distance. Shankar near the fence catches it easily. End of a big first wicket partnership. Can India build on this breakthrough?
Fifty for Seifert, his maiden in T20Is! Quicker one on the pads, Tim works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Munro misses out! Shortish ball in the line of the stumps, Colin stays back to pull it across the line but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It deflects to point.
Fullish and on off, Seifert pushes it firmly down to long on for a run.
The length continues to be on the shorter side. It's outside off, Tim cracks it off his back foot but finds the backward point fielder. Either side of him and it would have been another boundary.
SIX! This is very poor bowling. Keeping short and serving it on the hips of the batsman, Seifert just turns and dispatches it over deep backward square leg for a biggie.
EDGY FOUR! Short in length around off, not enough room, Seifert throws his bat at it and the outside edge flies wide of Dhoni to the third man fence. Boundaries continue to flow.
Play and a miss! Pandya pitches it up and outside off, Seifert winds up for a big heave-ho across the line but fails to make any connection.

A huge shout for LBW, turned down. The arm ball again, in line of the stumps, Seifert gets down to pull but misses. The ball hits him on the pads and up go the Indians. Going down leg mostly. A quick leg bye taken.
Again it's on the shorter side on off, Munro rocks back and punches it to sweeper cover. A single taken.
Short and on off, Seifert moves back and forces it through cover-point for one.
FOUR! Terrific improvisation. Full and around off, Seifert gets down and reverse sweeps it over backward point for a boundary!
Risky shot. The arm ball outside off, Seifert looks to initially drive, then decides to cut. Is late and the ball goes off the outside edge towards third man.
Short and outside off, slapped through the covers for a single.
Bunts it down in the direction of mid on and scampers across to the other end. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end. 66/0 in the Powerplay, a brilliant start for the Black Caps.
Too full in length and on middle, Seifert clips it through mid-wicket and collects a single.
FOUR! That's brutal! A slower delivery but on the shorter side outside off, Tim picks it early, goes on the back foot, waits for it and then slaps it through cover-point.
Slower in pace, on a length and following the batsman down the leg side, Seifert makes room but only hits it to point.
FOUR! Up and just over short fine leg! Once again it's a touch short and angling in on middle and leg, Seifert turns and pulls it over Khaleel inside the ring.
Poor delivery with fine leg up. Gets away with it. Only a run as Munro turns a shortish ball off his hips to deep square leg.
Wide called for height! Pandya digs in a short ball but it goes well over the head of the batsman.
Another bowling change. Hardik Pandya has the ball in his hand. Brothers bowling in tandem.
Quicker through the air, a touch short around leg, Munro moves back and punches it down through wide mid on for a run.

The arm ball now, outside off, Tim looks to defend but the ball comes in, skids through and almost goes through the gap between bat and pad. Takes the inside edge and goes to short fine leg. A single taken.
SIX! POUNDED! Full and around off, Seifert gets down and slog sweeps it way over backward square leg! That was hit beautifully. 50 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND INSIDE 5 OVERS!
Dropped by Dhoni! Flatter and shorter around off, Seifert tries to cut but it's too close to his body. It takes the outside edge, hurries behind to Dhoni who fails to hold on.
Goes down on one knee and sweeps it past backward square leg for a couple.
Short and around off, Seifert gets back and cuts it towards short third off the outside half.
Spin time! Krunal Pandya to bowl.
Shortish and around off, Seifert drags his pull shot off the inside half and it travels in front of square leg. A single to complete the over, 16 from it and 31 in the last two.
Up and over the infield! A slower one landing full on middle, Tim tries to flick but closes the face early. It flies off the leading edge over cover-point for a couple.
Beaten! This is excellent bowling. Khaleel slants across a back of a length ball around off and takes it away with the angle. Seifert tries to push it through the line but misses.
Not a bad reply by Khaleel. Spears this one in, a near yorker on middle, Munro pushes it back past the bowler towards mid on and pinches a run.
Fine leg pushed back. And what has happened here? The bails have come off. Heavy wind blowing across. Hope the dark clouds hovering over the stadium are blown over.
SIX! This one is flat! My goodness, Colin is so powerful. Khaleel alters his length to go short, pitches it wide outside off and Munro muscles it over point. The bowler is under immense pressure now.
SIX! That's gone the distance! The angle of the bowler assisted that shot. A slower one angling into the batsman from around off, Munro sits down on one knee and smokes it over mid-wicket.
Misses out there, Tim! Short and wide outside off, Seifert stays back and slaps it through the line. Fails to find the gap at point. Dot ball to end the over, 15 from it!
FOUR! That's crisply struck down the ground. Kumar angles in a full length ball around middle and off, Seifert clears his front leg and smacks it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Tim gets across the stumps a bit and taps it down to point.
SIX! PLUNDERED! The knuckle ball from Bhuvi but Seifert has picked it. A length ball, around off, Tim walks down the track and sends it over mid-wicket many a mile!

In the air... not timed that well and it falls safe! A touch short in length ball around leg, Colin comes down the track and heaves it over mid-wicket. It falls in no man's land in the deep and Rohit chases it down from mid on. Three taken.
A length ball sliding down the leg side, Munro swings his bat across the line but fails to make proper connection. It probably runs off his gloves to fine leg and they take a couple.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for a run.
Excellent bowling. Khaleel rolls his fingers over the ball and CM does not pick the slower one, at 121 kph. Swings hard but early and misses.
Fuller and wider outside off, Colin misses out. He slashes hard but cannot connect.
FOUR! No half measures. This is an overpitched delivery and now, Munro is ready. Waits for the ball to come in his zone and lofts it cleanly over mid off. One bounce and into the fence.

FOUR! Goes aerial but does not time it properly. A length ball outside off, Munro looks to go over mid off but mistimes it. Rohit Sharma gives it a good chase but fails to make a case. He dives near the ropes but in vain.
A length ball outside off, driven straight to cover.
Khaleel Ahmed to bowl from the other end.
Another flick, just one again. So that is 4 singles off the opening over. Decent start by Bhuvi.
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for one.
Around middle, worked towards mid-wicket for a run.
This one holds off the deck, Seifert looks to push but the ball comes on slowly, takes the outside edge and goes just wide of cover. A single taken to get the innings underway.
A length ball outside off, punched towards mid off again.
A length ball outside off, punched towards mid off.
Time to get underway. The Indian team is in a huddle now. Colin Munro and Tim Seifert are the Kiwi openers. Bhuvneshwar Kumar to kick off proceedings. A slip in place. All set, let's play...
National anthems going on currently. India's first followed by New Zealand's.

Pitch report - It's cold with strong wind blowing across the field says Simon Doull to begin with. Informs that 134 overs have been bowled so far on this surface. Mentions that there is a nice covering of grass and feels that there will be a little bit of slow turn. Doull is expecting plenty of runs but also suggests that playing through the wind will be a challenge for the batsmen.

New Zealand's skipper, Kane Williamson says that from the other night, just some subtle assessments need to be made in understanding the conditions and hopes that his unit is better prepared tonight. Informs that Daryl Mitchell makes his debut today, adding that Doug Bracewell and Jimmy Neesham miss out. Agrees that the change in squads is due to the change in format. Wants his side to play with freedom and express itself. On the fresh faces getting an opportunity, Williamson says that every chance one gets to play for his country needs to be cherished and one needs to enjoy himself.

India's skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they like to chase as a team and they have a good record doing so. Feels the pitch looks good and they are ready to see what target is set to them. Adds that they wanted to challenge themselves in the last game and hence chose to bat first in spite of early moisture in the surface but here it's a fresh start, different format and they are looking for a cracking beginning. Informs that they have a few new guys to play in this format, namely Krunal Pandya and Rishabh Pant.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it comes down in favour of the touring team. INDIA WILL FIELD!

Stat - In the last 5 T20Is, New Zealand have the letter W just once while India have the letter L only once. Easy to understand the in-form team then. However, in this part of the world, the Men in Blue are yet to win a match in this format. Is today the day?

Currently placed second in the T20I rankings, if India clean sweep the series, they will narrow the gap with their arch rivals who are atop while in case of New Zealand winning 3-0, they will jump from number 6 to number 3, provided Pakistan beat South Africa later in the evening. In the case of South Africa beating Pakistan and winning their series 3-0, the Black Caps will become 4th and India will slip to number 3. So, it might look an inconsequential drill to play this format with the 50-over World Cup fast approaching, but there is still plenty to look forward to. Stay tuned for more updates...

Apart from an aberration in Hamilton, it's been all India on this tour. New Zealand have failed to compete at the same level and there is a clear difference in quality between the two sides. But come the T20Is and that difference won't matter much. It's a format where most things are unpredictable and that's the beauty of it. The Men in Blue though still come across as a better-balanced unit compared to the Kiwis who will be without their most successful batsman in T20Is, Martin Guptill, and the in-form bowler, Trent Boult. So, what's going to be the script here in Wellington? Just wait and watch as we welcome you all for the coverage...
